reviewers.persona: Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: Both reviewers read every German string of the unit again. This covered title and title.canDo, spec.situation and the new spec.deviation, and the start: recapDe, the Folge title, its 9 lines and the gist item. It covered the LS1 and LS2 dialogues (10 lines each), the LS3 chat, the 6 H1 texts (27 lines), the strategy card and the 8 redemittel. For LS5 we read both speaking parts (situation, instructions, cards), aiRole, openingLine, the 8 hintWords and the 15 modelTurns. For LS6 we read the S1 task (title, situation, taskDe, 5 labels, checklist, model). We also read the 2 check lines, story.beat and the cliffhanger, every endLine and modelSentence, every explanation, the u01 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json, and the rule cards rc.praesens and rc.verbposition-2. We solved all 99 authored items blind from promptDe plus their options, tiles or audio line: start gist 1, input items 15, structured input 12, pool 37, reserve 15, exam 6, check 9, proof 4. We also solved the 5 form fields. For sentence_building we permuted the tiles and checked each V2 and V1 order against accepted[] and the prompt frame. We graded candidate answers with src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js itself (results quoted in previousFindings and F06). We compiled a1.1 into the scratchpad with node scripts/course-v2/compile.mjs a1.1 --out <scratch> --banks-out <scratch>, so nothing was written to the repo. We then ran the server's own normalizeSpeakingTask, buildCoursePartnerPrompt and criteriaPlan on the compiled a11-u01-s entry, and on a11-u04-s for comparison (F01). LEX-01 does not walk some surfaces: recapDe, the Folge title and lines, story.beat, the cliffhanger, openingLine, hintWords, modelTurns, the strategy card, redemittel, the S1 title/situation/labels/model, step titles, modelSentences and readAloud lines. We measured unknown tokens on them with the validator's knownForms, licensedForms, knownCompound and INSTRUCTION_METALANGUAGE. We recomputed word counts with the validator's wordCount: h1 46/46/36/38/36/51, S1 situation 36, LS3 chat 110, Folge 85, cliffhanger 22, Sp1/Sp2 situations 28/29. We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: h1 = 6 × abc, 3 options, 2 plays, [32–53] words; sp1 = monologue from a keyword sheet, rubric sd1-sp1 with 3 criteria; sp2 = cards-ask, 2 rounds, 2 points per question and 1 per answer, 6 in all; s1 = a 5-gap form with a situation of [36–48] words. We also checked them against the rubric files sd1-sp1, sd1-sp2, sd1-s1, course-micro and course-micro-sp. We read the grammar ceiling against grammar-spine.json and curriculum/a1-1.md §6 U1 and §9, and the new-word load against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32 new entries, productive share 0.5, sentences ≤ 12 words). We read the can-dos against registries/cando/a1.json. We checked the cast against casts/a1.json and series.json: languages, origins, Uwe Richter's office role and the voices. We checked the story against u02 (Empfang, „Neir“), u03 (Satzmelodie in LS1, „Wie geht's?“) and u12 (Wortakzent in LS1), each of which the new deviation cites. We re-read the u04 exemplar and its five review rounds and checked each of their finding classes here (see notes). No 360 px walkthrough was run; that is the walkthrough reviewer's remit.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 2 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 7 MINOR. The unit's own content is much better than in r1. 12 of the 16 r1 findings are fixed or fixed in the unit, the German on every unit surface is correct, and du/Sie is right everywhere. Every one of the 99 keys is right. H1 and S1 are exact to sd1.json, and every German-only task surface now uses known words. What stops exit lies mostly outside the unit file. (1) The Sprechen fix does not reach the learner (F01, blocker, class). The speaking functions ignore `parts`, although SCHEMA §12 says they read them. The AI partner is therefore given only the Teil 1 monologue script, without the learner's Teil 2 cards. The whole session is then graded with sd1-sp1 alone, which still scores „buchstabieren“ and „nummer“. So the new Teil 2 round is neither run nor scored, and a flawless session shows at most „1 von 3“. The same defect sits in 8 A1.1 units, including the u04 exemplar. That makes it a stop-the-line class: A1.1 cannot be declared finished until the engine reads `parts`. (2) The validator is red with 3 blockers (F02). lx.geschafft was allocated to u01 after r1 but is neither listed nor used, and specs.json still describes the pre-r1 Sprechen. (3) Two owner-held MAJORs from r1 are untouched. The u01 word card still says Emre speaks English (F03). The LS2 rule card still models „Was sprechen Sie?“, and rc.praesens still reads like „du sagen“ (F04). The minors are residues: the lexicon roles and load, 5 small item points, one formula item in H1, 5 small scene breaks, 5 small wording and look-ahead points, detector noise, and the missing verb-ending ErrorTag.

findings.quote: The compiled a11-u01-s has at its top level { template: 'sd1.sp1', mode: 'monologue', profile: 'sd1-sp1', parts: [ …sp1…, …sp2 cards „Kurs – Land“, „Sprachen – Englisch“… ] }. normalizeSpeakingTask(entry) → mode 'monologue', profile 'sd1-sp1', cards { learner: [], partner: [] }, situationDe '', instructionsDe ''. criteriaPlan(sd1-sp1) → vorstellen 1 · buchstabieren 1 · nummer 1 (target 3). findings.problem: The unit half of the r1 fixes has landed. Sp1 is marked 'reduced', the persona says „Nur die Vorstellung“, and an sd1.sp2 round now carries the Aufgabe proof of cd.a1.person-erfragen and cd.a1.verabschieden. None of it reaches the session or the result. The compiler writes `parts` into the bank and copies only parts[0]'s template, mode, profile and prepMinutes to the top level. The speaking functions read only that top level: normalizeSpeakingTask has no `parts`, and SCHEMA §12 says they read them. Run on the compiled entry, this has two effects. (1) The AI partner gets Teil 1's monologue script with no SITUATION and no AUFGABE. It never sees the learner's Teil 2 cards; only its own cards appear, inside the persona prose. It is told to ask follow-up questions after the monologue, not to answer card questions and then ask its own. SpeakingTaskView meanwhile shows the learner both parts and their cards. (2) The whole transcript is graded with sd1-sp1 alone. The Teil 2 questions and answers (sd1-sp2: 2 per question, 1 per answer, 6 in all) have no criterion. buchstabieren and nummer are still scored, although the unit tells the learner they come in Einheit 2: sd1-sp1.json is unchanged and appliesTo() knows only 'targets', so the rubric/grader half of r1-F01 has not landed either. A flawless session therefore shows at most „1 von 3 Punkten (Richtwert)“. That is a scorer on the wrong pass rule for both Teile (§9.4 BLOCKER). It also means the interaction can-dos the unit now performs correctly depend on an AI that is not told to run that Teil. The class is wider than u01. Eight A1.1 units carry a multi-Teil task: u01, u04, u05, u06, u08, u09, u10 and u12. In the u04 exemplar the session is graded with sd1-sp2 only, and its Sp3 request round is neither prompted nor scored. A class in ≥ 3 units of a level is stop-the-line (§9.4). Even once `parts` are read, MODE_RULES['cards-ask'] has the learner ask all their cards first and answer afterwards. The unit's model and SD1 itself alternate topic by topic.
findings.fix: Engine owner (E1 server track). normalizeSpeakingTask keeps `parts`, normalising each part. buildCoursePartnerPrompt renders one ABLAUF per part in order, with that part's situation, instructions and both card sets, plus a hand-over line („Jetzt Teil 2: …“). cards-ask runs round by round: the learner asks with the round's card, the partner answers, the partner asks with its card, the learner answers. speakingV2 grades each part with its own profile and sums the scores; ResultCard shows the score per Teil. Rubric owner (r1-F01, still open). A SpeakingPart declares the criteria it elicits (e.g. `criteria: ["vorstellen"]`), or buchstabieren and nummer get `appliesIf: 'full'` and appliesTo honours it when the Prüfungsfokus length is 'reduced'. u01 is then scored out of 1 + 6. Unit: no further edit. After the engine fix, play one session to check that the AI runs Teil 2 with the learner's cards and ends with „Danke! Auf Wiedersehen!“, and that the result card shows both Teile. No A1.1 unit with a multi-Teil task can exit before this lands, and u04's approval should be re-opened on this point only.
findings.proposedRule: A test over every compiled speaking bank (tests/course-v2-ai.test.mjs, or an EXM rail on the compiler output), covering each entry with `parts`. (a) buildCoursePartnerPrompt(entry) contains one ABLAUF per part and every part's learner and partner cards. (b) The grading plan covers every part's profile and scores no criterion the part does not elicit: sd1-sp1 in a 'reduced' Prüfungsfokus slot has max 1. Failing fixtures: a11-u01-s (monologue prompt, max 3 on sd1-sp1) and a11-u04-s (Sp3 unscored). The test runs over all registered courses.

exitCheck.note: Exit needs 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, every criterion ≥ 4 and ≤ 5 logged MINOR. F01 is the gate. It needs the E1 server track (read `parts`, one prompt and one score per Teil) and the rubric owner (a reduced criteria scope for sd1-sp1). It blocks every A1.1 unit with a multi-Teil task, not only u01, so A1.1 cannot be called finished before it lands. F02 is two unit edits plus the specs.json copy. F03 and F04 are one lexicon line and two rule-card lines. The unit-side edits are F02, F06, F07, F08, and the unit parts of F05 (ls1-l01) and F09 (ls1-l07, -l09/-l10, ls2-l05). Once they and the owner fixes are made, the unit carries 4 owner-held minors (F05 lexicon, the F09 spine/SCHEMA parts, F10 rule-smith and spine, F11 SCHEMA owner), within the limit. Re-review only P (play one session after F01 and read the result card), D and K, plus validate.mjs green. Class findings for the rule-smith: F01 (compiled-bank test), F04 (GRM-05), F05 (LEX-03), F10 (GRM-04/LEX-01 fixtures), F11 (ITM-12).

notes: Exemplar classes (u04 r1–r5) that do NOT recur. Dictation sources carry no `say` (r2-F01); the four u01 sources and c08 are plain lines. Number words are not rejected: f5 is now exact 'name' and „1“/„eins“ are correctly wrong (r3-F01). Key positions: the player seeds non-exam options, and H1 keys are 2/2/2 with no ascending-option pattern (r4-F03, r2-F04). Every fix proposed here was checked against the rails before it is recommended. We checked the ≤ 90-character rule for ls1-p11 (62) and ls2-mo (69), the word band [3, 16] for ls2-mo, TXT-03 line and word counts for the ls1-l09/-l10 swap, the known-word status of every inserted word („Anmeldung“ and „schreibt“ are not, which is why F09 asks for a gloss rather than a rewrite), and ruleCardMaxWords 60 for rc.praesens. We also checked the cast bible for every fact. One r1 proposal of ours produced a residue that this round logs: „Meine Muttersprache ist …“ in F09. Another, the r1-F11 rewording of ls3-i05, lost its „im Chat“ scope (F08).

Legal and claims: there is no outcome promise, no human-feedback claim and no exam-mark misuse on any surface. The AI role is „Gesprächsleitung (KI)“, and the H1 strategy card honestly says the exam uses pictures. Every exam task is original in the SD1 format. The one Landeskunde gloss („Grüß Gott = hello (in Austria and southern Germany)“) is correct, and the unit makes no other factual claim, so facts[] may stay empty. „der Kosovo“ as a Land matches Germany's recognition.
